program.fullbody2.day.0.name: Full Body — A
program.fullbody2.day.1.name: Full Body — B
program.fullbody2.description: For anyone with two free evenings a week. Every workout hits the whole body, so missing one doesn't leave a muscle group untouched for two weeks. Two days is thin, but it works — three will be better once you've got the time.
program.fullbody2.name: Full Body — 2 Days
program.fullbody3.day.0.name: Full Body — Day 1
program.fullbody3.day.1.name: Full Body — Day 2
program.fullbody3.day.2.name: Full Body — Day 3
program.fullbody3.description: The classic starting split. Three similar full-body sessions a week (Mon/Wed/Fri works). Compound lifts, minimal isolation — you groove the technique fast and add weight just as fast.
program.fullbody3.name: 🌱 Full Body — 3 Days
program.glutes3.day.0.name: Glutes — Heavy Day
program.glutes3.day.1.name: Legs — Quads
program.glutes3.day.2.name: Glutes + Light Upper
program.glutes3.description: Lower body gets three days, upper body the bare minimum so it doesn't fall behind. Glutes work in two modes: bridges and kickbacks hit them directly, deadlifts and lunges stretch them under load. Upper body stays light and goes last — it shouldn't eat into leg strength.
program.glutes3.name: 🦵 Glutes & Legs — 3 Days

program.split3.day.2.name: Legs + Shoulders
program.split3.description: Bro split: every workout is its own pair of muscle groups. Chest with triceps, back with biceps, legs with shoulders. Heavy volume on the target muscles and a full week to recover each.
program.split3.name: 💪 3-Day Split
program.strength5x5.day.0.name: Strength — Day A
program.strength5x5.day.1.name: Strength — Day B
program.strength5x5.description: Five sets of five, three big lifts a session, alternating day A and day B: A-B-A one week, B-A-B the next. No isolation on purpose — the whole point is adding 2.5kg to the bar every session, for as long as it keeps going up.
program.strength5x5.meta: beginners chasing strength · 3 workouts a week
program.strength5x5.name: 🏋️ Strength 5×5 — A/B
program.upperlower.day.0.name: Upper
program.upperlower.day.1.name: Lower
program.upperlower.description: Body splits into upper and lower, each trained twice a week. More volume per group than full body, easier to recover from than a daily split. Only got two evenings? Run the same two days once a week instead.
program.upperlower.name: Upper / Lower — 4 Days

push.newbie_nudge.1: YO ATHLETE! Account's set, log's still empty. The first entry is the easy part: come in and log a single set.
push.newbie_nudge.10: YO ATHLETE! Logging is easier than squatting: one message and you're done. Start with the easy part.
push.newbie_nudge.11: YO ATHLETE! I can total your tonnage, build your charts, and catch your records. Give me one set — I'll show you.
push.newbie_nudge.2: YO ATHLETE! Signing up was half the job. The other half's waiting at the gym. Let's go?
push.newbie_nudge.3: YO ATHLETE! I'm here, the log's open, and it's still at zero workouts. Start with anything — I'll count the rest.
push.newbie_nudge.4: YO ATHLETE! The log's waiting for its first entry. Doesn't have to be perfect — just first.
push.newbie_nudge.5: YO ATHLETE! You're signed up, no workouts yet. Fix that today?
push.newbie_nudge.6: YO ATHLETE! The first set doesn't have to be heavy — it has to be logged. Everything else builds from there.
push.newbie_nudge.7: YO ATHLETE! Every chart in this app starts from a single point. Put yours down today.
push.newbie_nudge.8: YO ATHLETE! An empty log is like a bar with no plates on it. Let's load the first workout?
push.newbie_nudge.9: YO ATHLETE! Every monster at your gym had a first log entry once. Yours is one set away.
push.plateau.1: YO ATHLETE! {exercise}, third session at the same weight — and over 12 reps every time. That's not a plateau, that's you holding back. Add weight.
push.plateau.2: YO ATHLETE! {exercise}: 12+ reps, three sessions straight, same weight. Your body's ready for more — time to load it.
push.plateau.3: YO ATHLETE! {exercise}'s clearly gotten easier — three sessions over 12 reps, same weight the whole time. Your body's ready for more.
push.plateau.4: YO ATHLETE! {exercise} has held steady for three sessions straight at 12+ reps. Time to move the weight.
push.plateau.5: YO ATHLETE! Three sessions of {exercise} with reps to spare — your body's asking for more load.
push.plateau.6: YO ATHLETE! {exercise}: weight's frozen, reps past 12 — three sessions straight. The next step's obvious, you just have to take it.
push.plateau.7: YO ATHLETE! By the numbers, {exercise} is too light for you now: three sessions at 12+ on the same weight. Try the next one up.
push.plateau.8: YO ATHLETE! {exercise}: three sessions on the same weight, over 12 reps every time. You've mastered this weight — time for the next step.
push.plateau.9: YO ATHLETE! You've outgrown {exercise}: 12+ reps, three sessions straight, same weight. The plates on the rack are waiting.
push.rank_near.1: YO ATHLETE! {missing} to the rank "{rank}". You're closer than you think. Finish it.
push.rank_near.2: YO ATHLETE! Next rank is "{rank}", and it's {missing} away. That kind of gap gets closed, not stared at.
push.rank_near.3: YO ATHLETE! {missing}, and "{rank}" shows up in your profile. A solid target for the next few days.
push.rank_near.4: YO ATHLETE! "{rank}" is already in sight from where you're standing: {missing}, and it's yours.
push.rank_near.5: YO ATHLETE! {missing}, and "{rank}" moves into your profile. I'll handle the move.
push.rank_near.6: YO ATHLETE! I ran the numbers: {missing} left to "{rank}". Numbers like that don't close themselves — but you will.
push.skip_10.1: YO ATHLETE! Day ten with no workout. That's not a pause anymore, that's a habit of not showing up. Breaking it today?
push.skip_10.2: YO ATHLETE! Ten days with no gym. A couple more, and you'll have to relearn how to walk in.
push.skip_10.3: YO ATHLETE! Day ten of downtime. Not rushing you — just pointing out the door's open.
push.skip_10.4: YO ATHLETE! Ten days of silence. The weights didn't grow, but they didn't run off either — right where you left them.
push.skip_10.5: YO ATHLETE! Day ten. Starting over is always harder than continuing — don't push it to day twenty.
push.skip_10.6: YO ATHLETE! Ten days off is a vacation at this point. Vacation's over.
push.skip_10.7: YO ATHLETE! Ten days. I've got your schedule memorized: empty, empty, empty. Let's rewrite it.
push.skip_10.8: YO ATHLETE! Day ten. The bar's standing right where it was and remembers your grip. Out of the three of us, you're the only one not showing up.
push.skip_10.9: YO ATHLETE! Ten days with no gym. Muscle memory's reliable, but it never signed up to wait forever.
push.skip_14.1: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks. I'm not lecturing, I'm counting days. The gym's still here. Where are you?
push.skip_14.2: YO ATHLETE! Fourteen days of silence. Enough already — come in, we'll sort it out there.
push.skip_14.3: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks without a single workout. Past this point it's not a pause anymore, it's a new habit. Which one do you want?
push.skip_14.4: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks with no gym. The first set after a break matters more than any other. It's waiting.
push.skip_14.5: YO ATHLETE! Day fourteen. I'll be honest: your form's started packing its bags. Stop it.
push.skip_14.6: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks is the line. Past it, people either come back or disappear. You're a come-back — I've seen your log.
push.skip_14.7: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks. I'm already telling the newbies about you like you're a legend. Show up before I start exaggerating.
push.skip_14.8: YO ATHLETE! Fourteen days. The log opens in two taps, the gym in one door. Check both.
push.skip_14.9: YO ATHLETE! Two weeks of silence. I get it — life happens. But life's easier when your back can hold it. Come back.
push.skip_3.1: YO ATHLETE! Day three with no gym. Rest or excuses — you sort that out. I just count the days.
push.skip_3.10: YO ATHLETE! Three days of silence. The membership runs even when you don't.
push.skip_3.2: YO ATHLETE! Three days of silence. Not lecture-worthy yet — but I noticed.
push.skip_3.3: YO ATHLETE! Three days without the bar. Not a tragedy, but not champion mode either.
push.skip_3.4: YO ATHLETE! Day three. The gym didn't move — you just didn't show up.
push.skip_3.5: YO ATHLETE! Day three. Two days is rest, three is a decision. Make the right one.
push.skip_3.6: YO ATHLETE! Three days and the log's gone quiet. Muscles are still fine. The habit's getting nervous.
push.skip_3.7: YO ATHLETE! Third day I'm staring at a blank page. Put a warm-up on it, at least.
push.skip_3.8: YO ATHLETE! Three days, no entries. The bar asked about you — I said you were busy. Don't make a liar out of me.
push.skip_3.9: YO ATHLETE! Day three. The couch counts as equipment too, but you won't build progress on it.
push.skip_5.1: YO ATHLETE! Day five with no gym. Muscles still remember how this works. The habit's starting to forget.
push.skip_5.10: YO ATHLETE! Day five with no gym. Some newbie's already eyeing your favorite bench. Come back — I'll get it for you.
push.skip_5.2: YO ATHLETE! Five days of silence in a row. Time to break it, not get used to it.
push.skip_5.3: YO ATHLETE! Five straight days with no gym. A bit more, and skipping becomes the habit.
push.skip_5.4: YO ATHLETE! Five days isn't a collapse, but it's a trend now. Stop it today.
push.skip_5.5: YO ATHLETE! Five days straight, no entry. Your form outlasts your motivation — but not forever.
push.skip_5.6: YO ATHLETE! Five days past the gym. The road there hasn't grown over — check for yourself.
push.skip_5.7: YO ATHLETE! Five days of rest, closed out. Open a working one — today's a good day for it.
push.skip_5.8: YO ATHLETE! Day five. Muscles are still calling this rest. By day six they'll call it something else.
push.skip_5.9: YO ATHLETE! Five days straight, not one entry. I checked — the log works fine. So it's not the log.
push.skip_7.1: YO ATHLETE! A full week off. The bar won't take it personally — it's iron. Your form will, and fast.
push.skip_7.10: YO ATHLETE! A week's gone. Good news: I'm still waiting for you. No bad news — just come in.
push.skip_7.2: YO ATHLETE! Exactly a week of silence. No lecture — just a reminder where the gym door is.
push.skip_7.3: YO ATHLETE! A week without a single set. Form doesn't wait — it's the first thing to go.
push.skip_7.4: YO ATHLETE! Seven days quiet — a full week. Time to bring the conversation back to the gym.
push.skip_7.5: YO ATHLETE! A week with no entries. Strength fades slow, habit fades fast. Get both back.
push.skip_7.6: YO ATHLETE! Seven days — a whole week. Good news: one workout and the counter resets.
push.skip_7.7: YO ATHLETE! A week ago you trained. Remember that feeling after? Still free of charge.
push.skip_7.8: YO ATHLETE! A week with no gym. I wiped the dust off your bar. Twice. Your turn now.
push.skip_7.9: YO ATHLETE! A week of silence. Your last record's already telling the gym it's in charge. Come argue with it.
push.streak_at_risk.1: YO ATHLETE! Streak on the line: {weeks} straight, and this week's still at zero. Time left: {days_left}. You built this streak — don't be the one who breaks it.
push.streak_at_risk.10: YO ATHLETE! You built that {weeks} streak one workout at a time, and it resets all at once. Time left: {days_left}. Don't hand it over.
push.streak_at_risk.2: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} without a miss — and it's all hanging by a thread right now. One workout keeps the chain going. Your call.
push.streak_at_risk.3: YO ATHLETE! One day left before the streak turns into "used to train." {weeks} is nothing to joke about.
push.streak_at_risk.4: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} straight is a schedule now, not luck. Zero workouts this week. Time left: {days_left}. Close it out.
push.streak_at_risk.5: YO ATHLETE! Time left: {days_left}, and the streak ({weeks}) still isn't extended. One workout decides everything.
push.streak_at_risk.6: YO ATHLETE! You showed up every week — {weeks} straight. This one's still empty. Time left: {days_left}. Don't let the counter reset.
push.streak_at_risk.7: YO ATHLETE! Your streak is {weeks}. One workout is all it takes to make it longer. Time left: {days_left}.
push.streak_at_risk.8: YO ATHLETE! A {weeks} streak is riding on one workout — the one you haven't done yet. Time left: {days_left}.
push.streak_at_risk.9: YO ATHLETE! I don't fudge the numbers: {weeks} straight, zero this week. Time left: {days_left}. Your move.
push.streak_milestone.1: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} straight without a single skip. That's not motivation anymore — that's character. Respect.
push.streak_milestone.2: YO ATHLETE! The streak just hit “{weeks} straight”. That's what regulars look like around here. Keep the pace.
push.streak_milestone.3: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} straight — milestone hit. I don't see streaks like this often, so I logged it separately.
push.streak_milestone.4: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} without a skip. Discipline is when you stop counting. I still count, though — and I'm proud.
push.streak_milestone.5: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} straight. I've seen plenty of guys in this basement: the ones who show up like this end up complaining their shirts got tight.
push.streak_milestone.6: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} straight. Motivation comes and goes — you just keep showing up. That's worth more.
push.streak_milestone.7: YO ATHLETE! {weeks} without a single skip. Weather changed, excuses were right there — and you showed up anyway. That's how it's forged.
push.weekly_digest.1: YO ATHLETE! This month you moved {tonnage} total — that's about {whale}. Come in, I'll show you the breakdown.
push.weekly_digest.2: YO ATHLETE! This week: {week_count}. Come in, let's see what's grown.
push.weekly_digest.3: YO ATHLETE! {best_day} is your most productive day on record. Keep it up?
push.weekly_digest.4: YO ATHLETE! 30-day total tonnage: {tonnage}. This week: {week_count}. Full breakdown's in the app.
push.weekly_digest.5: YO ATHLETE! Monthly tonnage: {tonnage}, and this week added up to {week_count}. Come in, see the whole picture.
push.weekly_digest.6: YO ATHLETE! Week's closed: {week_count}. Numbers are laid out in the app — come check them against last week.
push.weekly_digest.7: YO ATHLETE! Monthly total: {tonnage}. You lifted those kilos, I just kept the log. Come in for the details.
push.weekly_digest.8: YO ATHLETE! {tonnage} this month. Movers get paid for that kind of work — for you it just goes into a chart. Come take a look.
push.weekly_digest.9: YO ATHLETE! This week gave you {week_count}. I logged it, broke it down, and did the math — all that's left is for you to look.
push.win_back.1: YO ATHLETE! Three weeks — and that's fine. Everyone knows how to come back from a break. No excuses needed — come in, keep it light today, no heroics.
push.win_back.10: YO ATHLETE! The best day to come back was yesterday. The second best is today. There's no third on that list.
push.win_back.11: YO ATHLETE! A warm-up and two lighter sets, and you're back in the game. I'll do the counting, like always.
push.win_back.2: YO ATHLETE! Your last record is still here, waiting for you to come beat it. It's patient.
push.win_back.3: YO ATHLETE! Start light. The first step back after a break is the one that counts most. Let's warm up together.
push.win_back.4: YO ATHLETE! Three weeks is a long break, not a life sentence. Come in for even 20 minutes, no plan needed.
push.win_back.5: YO ATHLETE! Coming back doesn't call for heroics. Lighter weight, fewer sets — just start.
push.win_back.6: YO ATHLETE! The log remembers all your workouts, not just the break. Add a fresh one?
push.win_back.7: YO ATHLETE! Nobody's going to ask where you were. The gym doesn't ask questions — just open the door.
push.win_back.8: YO ATHLETE! Today's plan is simple: show up. Everything else is details, we'll sort it out there.
push.win_back.9: YO ATHLETE! The bar doesn't remember how long you were gone. It only remembers your grip. That hasn't gone anywhere.

rank.ladder_break_rule: A break costs one level at most — get back to your pace and the rank comes back too.
rank.ladder_explainer: Your rank is judged on three axes: total workouts, total weight lifted, and how often you train right now — over the last {weeks} weeks. It goes by whichever axis is weakest, so the other two can't carry it.
